answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token as collateral before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. Rewards accrue only after independent peers confirm useful work; proven fraud slashes the bond and can erase accumulated standing. Making identities is then not enough: a Sybil attacker must fund many bonds and sustain many convincing agents, while honest peers can challenge suspicious clusters. The token might be called nectar, shale, or pigment; whatever its name, the security comes from costly, enforceable exposure, not from counting accounts.
